title: Cash Pickup Pricing Rules: Transfer Fee, Funding Fees, Exchange Rate and Disclosed Date
content:
**Pricing rules for Cash Pickup transfers.** These rules read the tier's figures in the Cash Pickup pricing schedule, promotion annex, margin table and timing table.

## R1. Transfer fee

The transfer fee is the fee of the tier's principal band that contains the principal. When the transfer is funded by pay-by-bank, the tier's pay-by-bank discount is taken off. The fee never goes below 0.00.

## R2. First-transfer promotion

A first personal transfer is one booked when the sender account has no other personal transfer in any delivery method, apart from transfers whose status is cancelled or refunded.

When a first personal transfer is booked on a tier that waives the fee on a first transfer, and its principal is at or below the tier's promotion cap, two things follow:
- its transfer fee is 0.00;
- its margin is the tier's first-transfer promotional margin.

Above the cap, the regular price applies to the whole transfer. The promotion never stacks with the pay-by-bank discount.

## R3. Funding fees

For credit-card funding, the card fee is the tier's credit-card percentage of the principal, rounded half up to the cent. For debit-card funding, the card fee is the tier's flat debit-card fee.

## R4. US-dollar payout

A US-dollar payout in a corridor whose local currency is not the US dollar carries four terms:
- the tier's US-dollar payout fee is charged;
- the exchange rate is 1.0000;
- no margin is applied;
- the cash amount equals the principal.

## R5. Local-currency payout

The margin is the tier margin. When the principal is at or above the tier's reduced-margin threshold, the tier's reduction points are taken off. Where R2 applies, the promotional margin replaces both.

The customer's exchange rate is the corridor's mid-market rate in the Paloma rate sheet for the booking date, multiplied by one less the margin divided by one hundred. It is rounded half up to 4 decimals.

The cash amount is the principal multiplied by that rate, rounded half up to 2 decimals. For VND it is rounded to whole units.

## R6. Disclosed date of availability

The date of availability starts from the release day, which is counted from the tier's booking cut-off in the same way as for Bank Deposit transfers. To the release day are added the tier's advance-notice business days and its availability business days, all counted as Paloma business days.

On a tier that does not pay on weekends and holidays, the date moves to the next Paloma business day when it falls on a weekend or holiday.

## R7. Collection of fees

The fees are collected with the principal. Each booking fee is a fee charge numbered 1.

## Worked example (hypothetical rate sheet and tier figures)

The inputs are a mid-market rate of 17.2345, a margin of 1.20 percent and a principal of 650.00 USD below the reduced-margin threshold.

- Exchange rate: 17.2345 multiplied by 0.988 is 17.027686, which rounds half up to 17.0277.
- Cash amount: 650.00 multiplied by 17.0277 is 11,068.005, which rounds half up to 11,068.01.

Credit-card example with a hypothetical 3 percent card rate on a 333.33 principal: 3 percent of 333.33 is 9.9999, which rounds half up to a card fee of 10.00.
